default_q1.transcription: Object-Oriented Programming is a way to organize code using objects. The four principles are encapsulation (hiding data), abstraction (simplifying complex things), inheritance (reusing code from parent classes), and polymorphism (one interface, many forms). For example, a Car class can inherit from Vehicle class.
default_q1.reason: Student demonstrates good understanding of OOP concepts with clear examples. Minor deduction for organization and depth of explanation.

default_q2.reason: Excellent implementation with correct logic and clear time complexity explanation. Well-written code with proper variable names.

default_q3.transcription: डेटाबेस नॉर्मलाइज़ेशन डेटा को व्यवस्थित करने की प्रक्रिया है जो redundancy को कम करती है। 1NF means atomic values with no repeating groups. 2NF means 1NF plus no partial dependencies on composite keys. 3NF builds on 2NF but definition is slightly incomplete.
default_q3.reason: Good explanation of normalization and clear understanding of 1NF and 2NF. Student demonstrates conceptual understanding in bilingual format.

default_q4.transcription: OSI model has 7 layers: Physical transmits raw bits, Data Link handles node-to-node framing, Network provides packet routing via IP, Transport ensures reliable end-to-end delivery (TCP/UDP), Session establishes and ends connections, Presentation manages syntax and encryption, Application provides interface to software applications.
default_q4.reason: All 7 layers identified with correct functional descriptions. Concise and accurate.

default_q5.transcription: TCP is reliable, connection-oriented, and provides ordered data transmission with flow and error control. UDP is connectionless, fast, but does not guarantee packet delivery. TCP is used for HTTP/HTTPS, SSH, email, and database connections. UDP is ideal for VoIP, video conferencing, and online games where low latency is critical.
default_q5.reason: Clear distinction and practical real-world use cases given for both protocols.

default_q6.transcription: Stack follows LIFO (Last In First Out) principle like a stack of plates - the last plate placed is the first one removed. Queue follows FIFO (First In First Out) like a queue of people at a ticket counter. Stack examples: browser back button, undo/redo in code editors. Queue examples: printer spooler, OS job scheduler. स्टैक में सबसे ऊपर का आइटम पहले निकलता है जबकि क्यू में सबसे पहला आइटम पहले निकलता है।
default_q6.reason: Comprehensive explanation with accurate real-world examples and bilingual proficiency.

default_q7.transcription: SQL JOIN combines rows from two or more tables based on a related column between them. INNER JOIN returns only records that match in both tables. LEFT JOIN returns all records from left table and matched from right. RIGHT JOIN returns all from right table and matched from left. Example: SELECT employees.name, departments.name FROM employees INNER JOIN departments ON employees.dept_id = departments.id
default_q7.reason: Detailed description of all join types with a complete SQL syntax example.
